andhakavinda.notes: AN 5.114 and SN 6.13 explicitly locate the village in Magadha. The citations also pick up AN 5.113 and SN 6.12 and 6.14 on adjoining text. The occurrence in AN 5.120:3.2 is a chapter recap.

andhavana.notes: Sujato translates the name as ‘Dark Forest’, so the packet misses the grove even where the tap includes this sense. Examples include Kumārakassapa in MN 23:1.3, Sāriputta in AN 10.7:4.2, Rāhula in SN 35.121, and the sick Anuruddha in SN 52.10. AN 6.49:1.2 names the two residents as Khema and Sumana. DPPN calls the second monk Soma. AN 6.48, SN 35.120, and SN 52.9 are adjacent citation hits.

anejakā.notes: DN 20:15.6 names the Anejakā alongside the Accutā at the Great Assembly. DPPN gives DN ii.160, which lands in DN 16. The parallel citation in the Ariṭṭhakā entry gives ii.260 for this stanza.

annabhāra.notes: MN 77, AN 4.30, and AN 4.185 name the wanderer with Varadhara and Sakuludāyī. AN 4.28–29 and 4.184 are adjacent citation hits. Thag 16.9:19.1–2 names a different Annabhāra, the poor fodder carrier whom Anuruddha recalls having been. He has no candidate here.

anuruddha.notes: AN 1.192 names the disciple foremost in the divine eye. The episode of the great thoughts is AN 8.30. There Anuruddha reflects on seven in retreat and the Buddha supplies the eighth. DPPN attributes the meditation topic to Sāriputta. Several citations fall on neighboring discourses, including AN 8.29, MN 67, and MN 126. The packet also misses direct Pali addresses in SN 37.6–13 and the exchange with Sāriputta in SN 47.27:1.2–3, where the English is abbreviated.

anurādha.notes: SN 22.86 and SN 44.2 both give the wilderness-hut encounter at Vesālī. SN 44.1 concerns Khemā. SN 22.92 and SN 44.11 mention Anurādha in chapter recaps. The imported entry ends with stray ‘},’ characters.

anāthapiṇḍika.notes: AN 1.249 names Sudatta Anāthapiṇḍika as foremost among donors. DPPN combines details from two sickbed accounts. In SN 55.26:19 his pain subsides and he serves the elders a meal. In MN 143:16 the elders leave after teaching him and he dies shortly afterward. The citation for the protected mind is AN 3.109. AN 3.107–108 are adjacent hits.

araka.notes: AN 7.73:2.6–10 names Araka among the teachers of old, and AN 7.74 gives his teaching on the brevity of life. The identification with the Bodhisatta comes from the Jātaka account cited by DPPN.

ariṭṭha.notes: MN 22 gives the former vulture trapper's harmful view, and SN 54.6 gives the monk's account of breathing practice. SN 54.4–5 are adjacent citation hits. MN 116:4.1 explicitly calls Ariṭṭha a paccekasambuddha. DN 32:7.47 lists him with Sūra and Nemi in Vessavaṇa's realm. His office as messenger is an interpretation of that verse. AN 6.120–139:1.19 explicitly says upāsako. This lay follower has no candidate.

ariṭṭhakā.notes: DN 20:15.3 names the Ariṭṭhakā. Sujato reads the flax-colored gods in the following line as a separate group, the alternative DPPN attributes to Buddhaghosa.

aruṇa.notes: DN 14:1.12.4 calls King Aruṇa Sikhī's father. SN 6.14:2.1 uses the variant Aruṇavā. DN 20:17.1 lists the deities in ‘sukkā karambhā aruṇā’, translated as ‘the Dawn’. DN 20 is missing from the permitted list. Tapping aruṇā offers a separate DPD sense for this group, absent from the packet. Aruṇa 05 belongs under that sense when it is available.

aruṇavatī.notes: DN 14:1.12.6 and SN 6.14:2.2 both call Aruṇavatī the royal capital. The occurrence in SN 6.15:12.2 is a chapter recap.

asama.notes: SN 2.30:1.4 names the individual godling who praises Pūraṇa Kassapa. SN 2.29 concerns Susīma. DPPN's suggestion of a connection to the Asamā group is conjectural.

asamā.notes: DN 20:14.2 reads ‘asamā ca duve yamā’. DPD and DPPN take Asamā as a name alongside the twins, a reading also followed by Ṭhānissaro. Sujato renders asamā as ‘unequaled’ qualifying the twins. His note records the commentary's proper-name reading. This accounts for the empty mention list.

asibandhakaputta.notes: The headman appears throughout SN 42.6–9. These texts locate the Buddha at Pāvārika's mango grove in Nāḷandā. DPPN calls it Pārileyyaka. The question about helping the dead reach heaven occurs in SN 42.6, which the citation list misses. In SN 42.7:1.5 the claim about teaching some people less thoroughly is the headman's question. At 2.2, 2.6, and 2.10 the Buddha describes teaching the complete practice to each group.

asita.notes: MN 116:6.14 names the independent Buddha. MN 93:18.6 has asito devalo isi, translated as ‘the seer Devala the Dark’. The packet misses that sense's example and supplies no entry for him. Snp 3.11:1.4 also has Asito isi, the seer who visits the infant Gotama. His English name appears three segments earlier, and he too lacks a candidate.

asoka.notes: DN 14:1.11.1 identifies Vipassī's chief attendant, who lacks a candidate. Asoka 07 describes the deceased monk in SN 55.9:1.2 and 2.1. Its citation SN i.358 appears to mean SN v.358. SN 55.9:1.5 also names a layman Asoka. A single identification for the whole sutta would conflate the two men.

asokā.notes: SN 55.9:1.4 explicitly calls Asokā a bhikkhunī, and 1.6 names a separate upāsikā. Only the nun has a candidate. SN 55.10 is an adjacent citation hit.

assaji.notes: MN 35 gives the encounter with Saccaka. SN 22.88 gives the sickbed encounter that DPPN also attributes to this elder. The sutta itself calls the patient Venerable Assaji without further identification. MN 34 and SN 22.87 are adjacent citation hits. The other Assaji appears in the compound assajipunabbasukā in MN 70:4.1 and has no candidate here.

assapura.notes: MN 39:1.2 and MN 40:1.2 both name the Aṅgan town as their setting. DPPN describes both discourses. The citation list includes MN 38 and misses MN 40.

avanti.notes: The entry describes the country. DN 19:36.5 distinguishes the Avantis from their capital Māhissatī. The packet misses avantīnaṁ in the country lists in AN 3.70, AN 8.42–43, and AN 8.45. In AN 3.70 the English list is one segment earlier than the Pali. MN 108:2.1 concerns King Pajjota, the episode behind DPPN's citation. MN 107 is an adjacent hit.

avantiputta.notes: MN 84:2.1 names the king of Madhurā who visits Mahākaccāna. MN 83 is an adjacent citation hit.

avīci.notes: Iti 89:5.3 explicitly names the hell in Avīcinirayaṁ, a compound with its own dictionary line. The full DPPN entry cites Iti 89 in prose. DN 26:23.7 and AN 3.56:1.3 use avīci in descriptions of population density. MN 130 and AN 3.36 call the place of punishment mahāniraya. Its identification with Avīci there comes from the commentary.

ayojjhā.notes: SN 22.95:1.1 sets the foam discourse at ayujjhāyaṁ on the Ganges. That form opens the separate DPD headword ayujjhā, and Sujato spells the name Ayodhya. The variant accounts for the missing mention. For the log discourse, the app's SN 35.241:1.1 reads kosambiyaṁ, a variant DPPN itself acknowledges. SN 22.94 and SN 35.240 are adjacent citation hits.
